163428.name: Music Box, The Shadows Stir
163428.description: When activated, plays a music box arrangement of the haunting "The Shadows Stir" composition.

163429.name: Music Box, Enigmas of the Elder Way
163429.description: When activated, plays a music box arrangement of the mesmerizing "Enigmas of the Elder Way" composition.

163431.name: Music Box, Dreams and Memories
163431.description: When activated, plays a music box arrangement of the poignant "Dreams and Memories" composition.

163432.name: Music Box, The Merry Meadmaker
163432.description: When activated, plays a music box arrangement of the jaunty "The Merry Meadmaker" composition.

163704.name: Kingmaker's Trove
163704.description: Eye-catching, is it not? This gorgeous chest requires more than a second look to take in all its masterful filigree and accents.

163705.name: Warcaller's Painted Drum
163705.description: No musical instrument collection is complete without this massive drum. When used, all who hear it feel its beat deep within their bones.

163706.name: Dwemer Star Chart
163706.description: Show off your love of Dwarven astronomical knowledge by placing this wondrous star chart in your home.

163707.name: Antique Map of Glenumbra
163707.description: This detailed map highlights the complex topography of Glenumbra thanks to the artistry of the cartographer who crafted it.

163708.name: Antique Map of Stormhaven
163708.description: Even early maps of Stormhaven like this one show population centers, making the map a window into the past.

163709.name: Antique Map of Rivenspire
163709.description: Somehow the cartographer behind this map accurately rendered Rivenspire in great detail through all its gloom and fog.

163710.name: Antique Map of Alik'r Desert
163710.description: This map maker's aesthetic depicts the vast desert of Alik'r in gentle flowing lines, representing dunes that have long since shifted.

163711.name: Antique Map of Bangkorai
163711.description: The entire region of Bangkorai is shown on this antique map, though much of the detail is focused on the daunting Bangkorai pass.

163712.name: Antique Map of Stonefalls
163712.description: Though the ashfall may obscure the features of Stonefalls, the clear lines of this map are an able guide.

163713.name: Antique Map of Deshaan
163713.description: The fertile plain of Deshaan stretches out on this artful map.

163714.name: Antique Map of Shadowfen
163714.description: On this aged map, someone took great pains to depict the common paths and hazardous areas of the mire called Shadowfen.

163715.name: Antique Map of Eastmarch
163715.description: A master cartographer lent their skills to the crafting of this map of Eastmarch untold years ago.

163716.name: Antique Map of The Rift
163716.description: Despite its name, the sweeping temperate zone called the Rift is a hospitable place for Nords to come together, and this map points the way.

163717.name: Antique Map of Auridon
163717.description: One of the Summerset Isles, Auridon is painstakingly rendered on this map to the exacting standard of the College of Sapiarchs.

163718.name: Antique Map of Grahtwood
163718.description: Careful attention was paid to marking the well-trod footpaths through the old growth of Grahtwood.

163719.name: Antique Map of Greenshade
163719.description: Nearly a work of art in itself, this map of Greenshade provides some insight into what the region might have looked like in an earlier time.

163720.name: Antique Map of Malabal Tor
163720.description: The cartographer paid special attention to the coast and waterways of Malabal Tor when rendering this map.

163721.name: Antique Map of Reaper's March
163721.description: Skillful strokes create the boundaries and landmarks of Reaper's March on this map.

163722.name: Antique Map of Tamriel
163722.description: Though it details only major settlements and provincial boundaries, this continental map of Tamriel makes a good frame of reference for world travelers.

163723.name: Antique Map of Wrothgar
163723.description: The treacherous mountains of Wrothgar are expertly depicted on this map, though safe passage through them is anyone's guess.

163724.name: Antique Map of Vvardenfell
163724.description: The vastness of Red Mountain is truly apparent in this scale map of Vvardenfell.

163725.name: Antique Map of Summerset
163725.description: While one wouldn't want to use this map for navigation, given its age, it makes for excellent wall art.

163726.name: Antique Map of Murkmire
163726.description: The surveyor who succeeded in mapping the impenetrable marshlands of Murkmire made certain to note the migration of swamp leviathans.

163727.name: Antique Map of Northern Elsweyr
163727.description: The lands of Anequina and its majestic aqueduct are the subject of this skillfully illustrated map.

163728.name: Antique Map of Southern Elsweyr
163728.description: The kingdom of Pellitine stretches out like a lazing senche on this artistically rendered map.

165568.name: Ancient Nord Gate
165568.description: This is a large house item.

165569.name: Soul-Sworn Thrall
165569.description: This weak-willed fool is sworn to you for all time, and may be attacked or fed upon. Death cannot free them from this eternal bargain, and they will reanimate shortly after being slain. |cFFFFFFWhen placed in a home, Vampires may feed on the thrall.|r

165578.name: Basin of Loss
165578.description: This ancient font serves as a repository for centuries of vampiric ichor. |cFFFFFFWhen placed in a home, Vampires may offer their essence to the fountain and reduce their Vampirism Stage by 1.|r

165848.name: Font of Auri-El
165848.description: Nestled inside this massive stone edifice shines a glowing symbol of Auri-El, King of the Aldmer.

165849.name: Echoes of Aldmeris
165849.description: This triptych may stir ancestral memories in Mer—a longing of the soul for home. Or so the antiquarian claimed.

165850.name: Mnemonic Star-Sphere
165850.description: Experts continue to deduce the purpose of this device, but for now it serves as a memorable decoration.

165851.name: Sixth House Ritual Table
165851.description: Scholars of House Dagoth would find this ornate table both beautiful and thrilling—a marvel to admire, far away from Ordinators.

165852.name: St. Nerevar, Moon-and-Star
165852.description: Behold the Champion of Azura, the Hero of Red Mountain, the Herald of the Triune Way, Saint Nerevar Moon-and-Star in all his glory from the comfort of your own home.

165853.name: Moons-Blessed Ceremonial Pool
165853.description: Khajiiti legends claim that moon sugar comes from the light of the Two Moons trapped in the blessed waters of their homeland. The wondrous twinkling of this moonpool would lead you to believe it.

165854.name: Nisswo's Soul Tender
165854.description: This pedestal is considered sacred to the "nothing speakers" of Sithis, but it is believed to play a part in the eternal cycle of creation and destruction.

165855.name: Noble Knight's Rest
165855.description: Become the caretaker of this knight's sarcophagus and remains—but take your duties to heart lest you end up haunted!

165856.name: Sacred Chalice of Ysgramor
165856.description: Whether you choose to honor the Harbinger by keeping this chalice on display or by filling it with the best mead in Skyrim, it will serve you well.

165857.name: Brazier of Frozen Flame
165857.description: With its dazzling mix of sapphire and silver hues, this brazier lights up dramatically with an icy blaze.

165858.name: Coil of Satakal
165858.description: Call guests to dinner with this stunning ceremonial gong. Just don't be surprised if your guests aim to consume more than what you prepared.

165859.name: The Dutiful Guar
165859.description: This guar looks so real it could draw breath, leading some to suggest the subject of this piece lies beneath the bronze.

165860.name: Eight-Star Chandelier
165860.description: Brighten up a large space with this welkynd-stone chandelier dedicated to the blessed Eight.

165861.name: Golden Idol of Morihaus
165861.description: Winged. Golden. Arresting, as the demigod himself. Kneel before this idol and pray for a fraction of his might!

165862.name: Moth Priest's Cleansing Bowl
165862.description: Don't mistake this humble bowl as a simple object of sanitation! This cleansing bowl is believed to have removed impurities from the fingers of Moth Priests before they went about reading the Elder Scrolls.

165863.name: St. Alessia, Paravant
165863.description: Paravant, meaning "The First," is a title given to Alessia, leader of the rebellion against the Ayleids. Perhaps you'll be the first to display "The First," eh?

165864.name: Blessed Dais of Almalexia
165864.description: Elegant. Grand. Pointed. Much like Almalexia herself. Woe unto those who would let this blessed dais fall into dust and disuse.

165865.name: Beacon of Tower Zero
165865.description: Long removed from the Direnni Tower, give the holy light of Ada-mantia a place to shine forth from your abode.

165866.name: Ashen Infernace Gate
165866.description: Foreboding and grim, this gate emanates a sense of danger and gloom. Are you fearless or foolish enough to welcome whatever might pass through it into your home?

165867.name: Cat's Eye Prism
165867.description: The strange stone on this pedestal appears to catch light as easily as it catches the eye, but how it does this remains a mystery.

165868.name: Moonlight Mirror
165868.description: Framed gorgeously, the moons dominate this mirror, making it more for gazing at than into.

165869.name: Maormeri Serpent Shrine
165869.description: The Maormer are said to tame the great serpents of the sea, but while such magnificent creatures may be out of reach, this winding statue is the next best thing.

165870.name: Daedric Pillar of Torment
165870.description: Piece of art? Or torture device? Maybe both, depending on how you choose to view it.

165871.name: Carved Whale Totem
165871.description: Crafted from opal, this whale totem expresses a sense of simple joy to some. Others, however, believe it to hold more spiritual significance.

165872.name: Stained Glass of Lunar Phases
165872.description: The Khajiit describe the changing of the Two Moons as a graceful dance, and this stained glass window somehow captures their elegance, especially under the moonlight.

165873.name: Meridian Sconce
165873.description: It's said that the light of Meridia is boundless and eternal. Sadly, the candles in this majestic sconce are neither, but the impression this installation creates is long lasting.

165874.name: Jeweled Skull of Ayleid Kings
165874.description: If skulls feature prominantly in your decor, this jeweled skull can become the crowning piece of your collection.

165875.name: Ayleid Lightwell
165875.description: Ayleids believed that four elements composed Nirn: light, earth, water, and air. Light, when used in lightwells, allowed mages to restore their energy, though this one is primarily a showpiece.

165876.name: Ruby Dragon Skull
165876.description: The size and luster of this ruby would be a magnificent addition to any Dragon's hoard, even if wasn't masterfully cut into their likeness.

165878.name: Dwarven Puzzle Box
165878.description: Is it a toy? A vault? A piece of an even more elaborate puzzle? No one will know until someone opens it.

165990.name: Mammoth Cheese, Pungent
165990.description: Some folk diplomatically state that mammoth cheese is an acquired taste. Others argue that its smell is not only pervasive but even aggressive—to the point that you don't need to eat it to taste it.

165991.name: Statue, Vampiric Sovereign
165991.description: The vile enchantments placed upon this statue make it a grim reminder of a vampire's power. Whether cloaked in bats, imbued with dark energies, or wreathed in flame, weak-hearted mortals will never forget the sight of it.

165992.name: Antique Map of Western Skyrim
165992.description: Explore the regions of Western Skyrim with this masterful map. Elevations, waterways, and roads may be a tad out of date.

165993.name: Antique Map of Coldharbour
165993.description: One might question the sanity of the cartographer of this map, but according to experts in planar travel, it's remarkably accurate.

165994.name: Antique Map of Craglorn
165994.description: The cartographer who worked on this antique map detailed the dry wastelands of Lower Craglorn and mountainous regions of Upper Craglorn with a deft hand.

165995.name: Antique Map of Cyrodiil
165995.description: Though currently ravaged by war, this map of Cyrodiil gives you a picture of earlier times in this region.

165996.name: Antique Map of the Gold Coast
165996.description: Though this antique map doesn't note it, the Gold Coast was once called the Strident Coast.

165997.name: Antique Map of Hew's Bane
165997.description: This rare map depicts Hew's Bane, also once called Khefrem's Boot, a peninsula on the south coast of Hammerfell.

166014.name: Shrine of Boethra
166014.description: Few can resist the instinct to tuck tail and scurry from this epitome of cool, feline ferocity on display.

166015.name: Sweet Khenarthi's Song
166015.description: The rich blues and golds of this tapestry, along with its subject matter, might just tempt you into hanging it opposite your bed, allowing it to be the first thing you see in the morning and last thing you see at night.

166016.name: Ice Statue, Cowering Wretch
166016.description: Oh, the ignominy! To be transformed into ice while hiding in fear along the Frozen Coast! And yet, that's exactly what happened to this unfortunate soul.

166017.name: Witch Pike, Quiescent
166017.description: This odd bundle of sticks, vines, and witch magic looks inert—even safely impressive—but is it?

166018.name: Doll, Heiruna
166018.description: This doll vaguely resembles a character from a popular Nord children's story, and it seeks a new home. Will you cuddle her?

166019.name: Replica Throne of Windhelm
166019.description: Enthrone yourself like a mighty Nord with this faithful replica of the stone throne of Jorunn the Skald-King! Wisdom suggests that you shouldn't irk the High King by trying to claim his title as well.

166020.name: Greymoor Keep Banner, Hanging
166020.description: A dramatic banner representing Greymoor Keep in Blackreach, that most fabled of places.

166021.name: Karthwatch Banner, Hanging
166021.description: With its knotwork tower, the gray banner of Karthwatch symbolizes the bravery and steadfastness of the Nords who live there.

166022.name: Morthal Banner, Hanging
166022.description: Morthal's banner features a white triskelion on a field of gray reminiscent of its misty marshes. Whether the triskelion symbolizes the unity of the mind, body, and spirit—or something else entirely—serves as the subject of scholarly debates.

166023.name: Solitude Banner, Hanging
166023.description: Throughout Solitude's long history, it has been watched over by the wolves on its banners. Legends claim that so long as one wolf flies on the ramparts of Solitude, Mara's protective embrace will grace the city's walls.

166024.name: Kyne's Aegis Banner, Hanging
166024.description: The Mother of Nords watches over those who display this colorful banner of the Hawk Ascendant—or so popular Nord sentiment claims!

166025.name: Nord Basket Trap, Fishing
166025.description: Though once used primarily by Nords in Western Skyrim, baskets such as this one catch fish well outside the Sea of Ghosts now.

166026.name: Nord Boat, Fishing
166026.description: Complete with netting and sails, this Nord fishing boat is a common sight on the Sea of Ghosts. Though many of those fisherfolk catch more than they bargained for in those treacherous waters, or so the stories tell.

166435.name: Seat of the Snow Prince
166435.description: The simple lines of this stone throne offer some insight into the personality of the Snow Elf ruler who ordered its creation.

166436.name: Tusks of the Orc-Father
166436.description: None who see these imposing tusks from Wrothgar on your estate can doubt your bravery. Having them is one thing. Keeping them? Another entirely.

166471.name: Tall Papa's Lamp
166471.description: The incense burned within this marvelous lamp is alleged to have guided Yokudans into transcendent experiences.

166472.name: Morwha's Blessing
166472.description: The four-armed Yokudan fertility goddess Morwha stands enshrined and flanked by her winged guardians, promising prosperity to all who stand before her.

166473.name: Greensong Gathering Circle
166473.description: With this cauldron, you can gather companions to honor the Green or simply display it as an interesting Wood Elf creation.

166474.name: Altar of Celestial Convergence
166474.description: What occurs when the stars align to match the constellation at the heart of this ominous altar remains a mystery, but the sinister serpents on display conjure only catastrophe in the imagination.

171387.name: Nighthollow Banner
171387.description: The banners of the Nighthollow clan have clung to the walls of their crumbling empire for thousands of years. May this one serve you equally as long!

171388.name: Dwarven Tonal Cascade
171388.description: "Dwemer devices are precise instruments. Usually. This, however, appears to emit tonal forces in a torrent. Catastrophically dangerous. Never turn it on. If there were a control mechanism, maybe, but I can't fathom what could tune it."—Neramo

171389.name: Dwarven Crystal Receptacle
171389.description: Though its pronged receptacle stands empty, this pillar once housed some form of Dwarven stone or crystal.

171390.name: Reachwitch Protective Totem
171390.description: This totem sees use only in places where Reach clans intend to set up camp for more than a few weeks or around Markarth. Some witches claim that subversive uses for this totem abound among bloodthirstier clans.

171391.name: Reach Effigy of Turnabout
171391.description: The bones, twigs, and hide that make up this effigy all receive blood-blessings from the clan's witchfolk, who claim it sends spirits with ill intentions back to plague their erstwhile masters.

171392.name: Falmer Totem of Dominance
171392.description: "I would ask the scholar who wrote 'I discovered Falmer mark their territory with such totems' more about this ill-scented column and these Falmer she mentions, but she died after penning this entry in her journal. How inconvenient."—Scholar Tuintaatel

171393.name: Tree, Reach Totem
171393.description: "Above us, the limbs stretch to the sky. Below us, the roots spread throughout the ground. Where both meet in this tree, place your bone offerings. Renew them with oils after every rain or the tree's spirit will seek your doom."—Reachwitch Eoinellgen

171394.name: Dwarven Stand, Void Crystal
171394.description: "Admittedly, I do love shiny things—perhaps too much given my time spent, ahem, among guards shall we say—but something about this stone makes me feel ill at ease. What were those barmy Dwarves up to with this?"—Gorthuth, Dwarven Ruins Delver

171395.name: Dwarven Beacon, Aetheric
171395.description: "By Dagon's fiery arse, the aetheric stones in this Dwarven device simply will not budge. What are they for? Don't care. But by Zen, I can't lug this entire piece of metal out of here right now. Feh."—Gorthuth, Dwarven Ruins Delver

171396.name: Dwarven Tonal Manacle
171396.description: "This Dwarven gewgaw tethers … something. Trust me, I know plenty about tethers. Can smell 'em on a guard at more than fifty paces away, and this thing reeks of tethers…manacles…that sort of thing. Let's avoid it."—Gorthuth, Dwarven Ruins Delver

171428.description: The dramatic reds and blacks of this stained glass form striking iconography, making it a must-have for any vampire seeking to decorate their sanctuary.

171429.name: Red Eagle Cave Painting
171429.description: Though this cave painting stands tall, the legend of Red Eagle stands taller still among those living in the Reach … and beyond. The visceral impact of this piece may just haunt your dreams.

171431.name: Antique Map of the Reach
171431.description: Reachfolk have little use for maps, knowing the land as well as they know their own bodies, so an intrepid explorer must have drafted this cartographic wonder—perfect for hanging on your wall or planning your next Reach excursion.

171542.name: Music Box, Farewell to Nenalata
171542.description: When activated, plays a music box arrangement of the wistful "Farewell to Nenalata" composition.

171543.name: Music Box, Feast of All Flames
171543.description: When activated, plays a music box arrangement of the playfully tumultuous "Feast of All Flames" composition.

171544.name: Comet, Aetherial
171544.description: "I can only speculate why the Ayleids sought to recreate the effect of a shooting star passing through the night sky. I set up a few in my garden to my guests' delight, after putting aside some for further study."—Mage Uryacil

171545.name: Ayleid Gate, Large
171545.description: Often found within Ayleid ruins, these large gates provide an elegant barrier between rooms. Whether they keep something in or out is entirely up to you.

171546.name: Ayleid Relief, Blessed Life-Tree
171546.description: "Each time I see the Ayleid life-tree, my heart beats faster. What treasure—what knowledge—lies deep beneath its roots? I put this relief in my home so I never forget that exhilaration!"—Theldyn Faden, Explorer

171601.name: Replica Jubilee Cake 2021
171601.description: Chef Donolon's Jubilee Cake is the perfect pastry to celebrate any special occasion or awesome anniversary. Relish its luscious flavor—tantalizing to your taste buds!

175700.name: Deadlands Chandelier, Caged
175700.description: Daedric flames burn within these ornate, caged sconces. The light they grant may seem harmless enough, but the fires of Oblivion often cast darkness upon the soul.

175701.name: Xi-Tsei Stone Idol
175701.description: Though no blood or moss mars this Argonian idol, similar symbols decorate the infamous Xi-Tsei xanmeer where the Fourth Imperial Legion met its end in 1E 2820. Did this particular stone guardian watch over the legion's bloody massacre? Who can say?

175702.name: Entwined Snakes, Crystal Holder
175702.description: An ancient Argonian artisan captured this endless struggle between fang-baring serpents, crafting a stone dance of poison and fang that can hold a crystalline light. The jaws of these snakes gape open, ready to hold another light source of your choice.

175703.name: Banner, Tattered Mehrunes Dagon
175703.description: Every ambitious soul needs grit to prevail—so it's fitting that grit worked its way deep into the fabric of this well-worn blood-red banner of the Razor Prince!

175704.name: Inert Oblivion Gate
175704.description: This foreboding structure once held the promise of entry to Oblivion, though now it stands curiously silent. Or does it?

175705.name: Deadlands Pillar, Tall Inscribed
175705.description: With its eerie crimson markings, this carved pillar brings the weighty and sometimes malice-laden presence of the Daedra to any area it dominates.

175706.name: Seal of the Ambitions
175706.description: This seal represents the vessels of Dagon's power, known as the Ambitions. May its commanding gaze serve as a reminder of all you accomplished against the Prince of Cataclysm!

175707.name: Banner of Leyawiin
175707.description: The spring green and glinting gold of Leyawiin's banner provide the perfect backdrop for the city's proud, equine emblem. Long may the White Stallion ride!

175708.name: Deadlands Tormentor, Chained
175708.description: Some say chains make for the best captive audience, and the ones on this Daedric-tested device of torment promise to keep your guests secure—and fettered.

175709.name: Deadlands Podium of Ruination
175709.description: Even the most delicate verse can take on an air of menace when you place it—preferably in weighty tome form—upon this imposing podium.

182302.name: Daedric Enchanting Station
182302.description: Who knows what vile enchantments took shape on this Daedric worktable? Perhaps you can craft something even darker. When placed in your home, this crafting station allows you to craft Enchantment items.

182303.name: Dagon's Scalding Gibbet
182303.description: Fear is a tool best used in moderation, but when you must turn to it, be ready with the appropriate accessories. This torture device, for instance—even looking at it may cause some to spill their secrets.

182304.name: Tree, Charred Dagonic
182304.description: How this skeleton of a burned tree once grew here remains a mystery.

182305.name: Deadlands Window, Stormglass
182305.description: While most associate Deadlands architecture with fiery reds, the deep blues of a churning sea are no less intimidating. Let the cold light of a rising flood wash over you when standing before this Daedric window.

182306.name: Daedric Altar, Mehrunes Dagon
182306.description: No place of worship dedicated to the Prince of Destruction can be called such without this altar. If you can't please Mehrunes Dagon, best make sure you don't anger him by lacking this centerpiece.

182307.name: Deadlands Lightning Rod, Etched
182307.description: If you dare to live among the storms of the Sever, be sure to place plenty of lightning rods around. The fact that these might scare off cowardly mortals is a welcome perk.

182308.name: Deadlands Wind Gate Pinion
182308.description: This majestic stone structure draws the gaze even as it dominates the landscape. Perfect as a focal piece in your courtyard or bit of Oblivion.

182309.name: Deadlands Buttress, Large
182309.description: Decorate and support your walls in Daedric style with this towering buttress. While it won't stop Dagon himself from entering your abode if he wishes, lesser beings might reconsider any plans to besiege your residence.

182310.name: Deadlands Buttress
182310.description: For those needing added structural support for their walls, this Daedric-themed buttress serves the purpose while adding a touch of dread to your home.

182311.name: Deadlands Platform, Octagonal
182311.description: Every second-rate baron needs a platform on which to stand. But why settle for second-rate mortal sovereignty when you can go full doom and destruction with this Daedric-themed platform?

182312.name: Deadlands Displacer, Inactive
182312.description: This inert displacer might not whisk you off to points unknown, but it will lend any room you place it in an air of arcane mystery!

182313.name: Portal Key Replica
182313.description: Though this item is a mere replica of a real portal key, the memories it unlocks for you can be priceless. Maybe a bit hair-raising, but definitely priceless.

182314.name: Deadlands Wall, Wide
182314.description: This is a large house item.

182315.name: Sulfur Pool
182315.description: Some of Madam Whim's clients swear by the relaxing properties of the mud from Deadlands sulfur pools. Others find these pools to be more useful than "keep out" signs. Which are you?

197700.name: Apocrypha Fossil, Bones Large
197700.description: Though you may not ever find out what creature these bones belong to, they're a must-have for any ossuary garden or, if you're more traditional in your reliquiae displays, fossil collection.

197701.name: Apocrypha Fossil, Nautilus
197701.description: Lovers of large fossils, rejoice! This enormous nautilus fossil can serve as the backdrop for your next outdoor gathering.

197702.name: Apocrypha Fossil, Worm
197702.description: Faithful of Mora believe that the fossils embedded across the realm of Apocrypha are remnants of another place, another realm, the origin point of the Daedric Prince of Knowledge. Certainly, they correspond to no creatures native to Tamriel.

197703.name: Apocrypha Fossil, Arch
197703.description: This arching fossil may have once belonged to a gigantic creature of Apocrypha, but now it can serve as an archway within your home.

197705.name: Telvanni Alchemy Station
197705.description: With components inspired by a variety of cultures, this alchemy station not only helps you mix all manner of ingredients into useful potions, but also adds a touch of all things Tamriel to your home.

197706.name: Trifold Mirror of Alternatives
197706.description: "May your wardrobe reflect the dark sophistication of this mirror trio. It's not my style, but when I look deeply into your eyes, I think it suits you more than you may think."—Fairwen of Vulkhel Guard

197707.name: Apocryphal Well
197707.description: The liquid in this well never stills and resembles a roiling portal to the realm of Hermaeus Mora.

197708.name: Cliff Strider Skeleton Stand
197708.description: Set up this experiment in taxidermy and Cliff Strider anatomy in your home—just make sure to warn any guests about it before they enter its space. It's a bit … startling.

197709.name: Tribunal Window, Stained Glass
197709.description: Bring the light of the Tribunal into your home with this stained glass window. Featuring rich colors, this sacred art piece can serve as the focal point of your personal shrine to ALMSIVI.

197710.name: Mushroom Classification Book
197710.description: Flip through the illustrated pages of this Telvanni library staple. While it may not share the deep knowledge that mycoturges possess, it can serve as an entertaining conversation starter at your next gathering.

197711.name: Antique Map of the Telvanni Peninsula
197711.description: The fine detail work on the coastlines contrasts strongly with inland portions of the map. Almost as if House Telvanni had little interest in a truly accurate depiction of the peninsula.

197712.name: Antique Map of Apocrypha
197712.description: "Mapping Apocrypha and expecting the result to help anyone else is foolish. Instead consider the map to be more of a visual guide to the cartographer's experiences there—unique to them alone."—Excerpt from an unknown Cipher's Journal

197713.name: Tribunal Rug
197713.description: This is a standard house item.

197715.name: Necrom Stele, Ceremonial
197715.description: Raised only to venerate ancestors that have shaped the very fabric of a family line. Ensure your forbearers are pleased by making this classic stele the focal piece of your own shrine.

197716.name: Crystalline Mind Barrier, Replica
197716.description: Replicated painstakingly via rough description by the very few that have returned from the nightmare realms of Vaermina, this barrier is a reminder of a dark and challenging mind-realm far from the light of day.

197717.name: Apocrypha Altar, Lighted
197717.description: Some scholars of Apocrypha claim that if you meditate at one of its altars, a stray piece of lost knowledge may find its way into your mind. Will this work in your home? Probably not, but you'd look suitably impressive while meditating.

197718.name: Necrom Archway
197718.description: Accents of green on white stone decorate this solid archway. Anything beyond it must surely be worth seeing given its elegantly dramatic appearance.

197719.name: Apocrypha Courtyard Pool
197719.description: The visions one could scry within the pools of Apocrypha sometimes cause a viewer's mind to shatter. Thankfully for you, this particular pool looks stunning, but provides no mind-breaking visions.

197720.name: Hermaeus Mora Banner
197720.description: No one can entertain doubts as to your affiliation when you hang this banner featuring the Golden Eye's symbols in your home.

197721.name: The Lord of Fate and Knowledge Frieze
197721.description: Place this frieze of the Keeper of Forbidden Knowledge in a prominent place. Perhaps the One Who Knows will look upon you with favor and share some curious bit of information when you most need it. Or, perhaps not.

197722.name: Apocrypha Portal Seal, Replica
197722.description: If this were a real portal seal in your abode, you may end up questioning your life choices. As it stands, this replica serves as a marvelous accent in any space.

197723.name: Apocrypha Stalk, Scryeball
197723.description: Feel as if you're being watched? With these bizarre stalks around, you are. Each stalk adds an element of oddball ambience to wherever you choose to plant it.

197724.name: Tales of Tribute Kit, Travel
197724.description: A testament to the increasing popularity of this Roister's club favorite, this travel kit shows your love of Tales of Tribute to all and sundry that visit your home.

197725.name: Replica Fateweaver Key
197725.description: A recreation by Azandar al-Cybiades to honor the research adventure of a lifetime.

197726.name: Dormant Tyranite Calx
197726.description: This broken, brittle shard of tyranite calx is empty of magic and cool to the touch. Should the metal's dormancy ever change, you will be the first to know.

204792.description: The unique design of this large table allowed the Five Companions to plan, debate, and share information before setting out on their next adventure. Perhaps some memories of past days linger, waiting for you to watch?

204793.name: Scholarium Column, Large

214355.name: Solstice Giant Crocodile Skull
214355.description: Among the Argonians of Solstice, the crocodile was seen as a guardian of the Unmaker, Sithis. This skull belonged to an enormous beast, likely reared by worshippers of the Dread Father to guard one of his temples.

214356.name: Solstice Giant Crocodile Ribs
214356.description: Among the Argonians of Solstice, the crocodile was seen as a guardian of the Unmaker, Sithis.  Ribs like these have been found in ancient ceremony sites dedicated to the Death-Dancer sect, a void-dwelling tradition dating back centuries.

214357.name: Solstice Giant Crocodile Tail
214357.description: Among the Argonians of Solstice, the crocodile was seen as a guardian of the Unmaker, Sithis. Enormous beasts like this once acted as mounts for Stone-Nest assassins in their ancient conflict with Coldharbour.

214358.name: Large Solstice Bismuth Tower
214358.description: An artifact of the incredible Stone-Nest Argonian culture. These ornamental towers once marked future locations for Xanmeers or temple support buildings, a discipline now lost to the artisans of today.

214359.name: Geometric Stone-Nest Totem
214359.description: An artifact of the incredible Stone-Nest Argonian culture. These simple totems were once wayfinders to sacred structures across Solstice. They have been moved so many times that it's impossible tell what they were originally pointing to.

214360.name: Stone-Nest Totem, Iguana
214360.description: An artifact of the incredible Stone-Nest Argonian culture. A representation of a simple lizard may seem ironic in a culture of lizard-folk, but these beasts were seen as sacred animals in the distant past.

214361.name: Stone-Nest Totem, Behemoth
214361.description: An artifact of the incredible Stone-Nest Argonian culture. Most likely an ancient representation of the dangerous Vahath Behemoth, a guardian beast created in the days of myth and legend.

214362.name: Stone-Nest Totem, Massive Skull
214362.description: An artifact of the incredible Stone-Nest Argonian culture. The skull of Sithis wears many shapes and has been worked into stone in a hundred different ways.

223868.name: Bearer of Fargrave, Broken Skull
223868.description: How the Bearers of Fargrave met their end is a mystery known to no mortal or Daedra yet living. It's said a great and terrible calamity occurred, the Bearers forgot their purpose, and they met their ends as aetherial sands rose to consume them.

223869.name: Imperial Titan Slayer

223870.name: Valenwood Skull Blocks

223871.name: Hourglass of Akatosh Brace, Massive

1.name: Mara's Kiss Public House
1.hint:
Purchase Requires:
"Room to Spare" House Quest Completion
1.description:
As the least restricted seaport in the Summerset Isles, Vulkhel Guard has visitors from across Tamriel—and you're likely to meet most of them hoisting a mug at the Mara's Kiss Pub.
Room is too small for Dueling.

2.name: The Rosy Lion
2.hint:
Purchase Requires:
"Room to Spare" House Quest Completion
2.description:
This inn has always had the reputation of being the safest place in Daggerfall for common citizens in search of illicit services to meet their shadier counterparts.
Room is too small for Dueling.

3.name: The Ebony Flask Inn Room
3.hint:
Purchase Requires:
"Room to Spare" House Quest Completion
3.description:
The Dark Elves may not worship Dibella, but down at the cornerclubs they show that they still know how to have a good time—in their own special way.
Room is too small for Dueling.

4.name: Barbed Hook Private Room
4.description:
Like every busy port, Skywatch has a seamy underside. A private room at the Barbed Hook offers easy access to the criminal classes—and a quick escape from the nearby docks.
Room is too small for Dueling.

5.name: Sisters of the Sands Apartment
5.description:
In Sentinel, the best way to hide out in plain sight is with a private room in the Sisters of the Sands, the town's largest inn. It also has the best food in the city, and is the place King Fahara'jad sends to for take-out.
Room is too small for Dueling.

6.name: Flaming Nix Deluxe Garret
6.description:
Even if you don't personally have a taste for the famous fire-pit dancing at the Flaming Nix, you have to admit it adds a certain cachet to having a room there. Not to mention an unusual fragrance.
Room is too small for Dueling.

7.name: Black Vine Villa
7.description: Would you want to live in an old stone house just across a dark jungle stream from a haunted Ayleid ruin? Silly question—who wouldn't?

8.name: Cliffshade
8.description: Just outside the Altmeri settlement of Marbruk, the forest is wide and open, the climate is mild, the setting idyllic: the elegant home of Cliffshade seems an abode blessed by the gods.

9.name: Mathiisen Manor
9.description: This elegant walled estate is truly the apogee of Altmeri architecture, including a grand entrance hall, curving double staircases, and a blossom-tree garden with circular reflecting pool.

10.name: Humblemud
10.description: A mud house is a constant reminder of the impermanence of life, and that we are but standing waves in the river of existence. But one still wishes it to look nice and comfortable, and decorates accordingly. Of course.

11.name: The Ample Domicile
11.description: "This house is a good house, plenty of room for guar! Palisade is strong to keep guar from straying, and many guar can feed in the garden! Very good, yes! Esqoo will come to visit often!" —Esqoo of Dhalmora

12.name: Stay-Moist Mansion
12.description: How does this spacious and comely hilltop manor, so far above the fen, nonetheless stay so delightfully damp? It is a paradox, like life itself. (Don't miss the upper-story lodging with separate entrance!)

13.name: Snugpod
13.description: A perfect graht-oak pod home, grown by a Home Singer from the very roots of Elden Root—compact, comfortable, and convenient to everything. Praise Z'en!

14.name: Bouldertree Refuge
14.description: When civilization grows too confining, it's a relief to be able to withdraw into a handsome home in the wilds—especially one with an imposing wall around it, to keep out beasts and bandits.

15.name: The Gorinir Estate
15.description: The Gorinir family, a cadet branch of the royal Camoran line, has fallen on hard times and had to sell their palatial Cormount home. The seasons turn, luck changes, and their loss is your gain.

16.name: Captain Margaux's Place
16.description: The famous Breton merchant-explorer Captain Margaux hasn't been seen since her ship the Golden Spriggan sailed off over the horizon into the Sea of Pearls—which makes her house near the docks in Daggerfall available for you!

17.name: Ravenhurst
17.description: Two floors, no waiting, in this handsome walled town house makes for prime real estate in the quaint Rivenspire town of Fell's Run. The local story that the ravens that loiter around the front steps are the revenant spirits of former owners is absurd.

18.name: Gardner House
18.description: The Gardners were the royal family of Wayrest before every single one of them was carried off by the Knahaten Flu. Which is why the spacious and well-situated Gardner House feels like it's fit for a king!

19.name: Kragenhome
19.description: This residence might not be in Kragenmoor's best neighborhood, but if you're looking for classic Dunmeri architecture at an affordable price, this town house certainly fits the bill.

20.name: Velothi Reverie
20.description: This charming abode was named after both the Prophet Veloth who founded the surrounding town of Narsis, and the Velothi Mountains that rise above the walled garden at its rear.

21.name: Quondam Indorilia
21.description: This capacious Dunmeri mansion, with its walled garden and view across a waterfall to majestic Mournhold, was originally built to house a noble family of House Indoril.

22.name: Moonmirth House
22.description: A small elevated house on an idyllic plantation in the mild and hospitable clime of Khenarthi's Roost? This one would find that sweet paradise!

23.name: Sleek Creek House
23.description: All your friends are already nearby in Rawl'kha, yes? Invite them over to have a party at your so-sleek riverside house, with its private garden and over-creek deck. Much sweetness!

24.name: Dawnshadow
24.hint:
Gold Purchase Requires:
"Reaper's March Adventurer" Achievement
24.description: Ah, such a sweet estate, with every appurtenance—out in the country, yet convenient to the nearby Khajiiti metropolis of Dune! What can one do but love and admire it?

25.name: Cyrodilic Jungle House
25.description: An Imperial, of course, is at home anywhere in Tamriel. This compact house at the Baandari Trading Post in Malabal Tor is a bit of Cyrodiil in Valenwood, and just steps away from the fine food and drink at the Silver Moons Inn.

26.name: Domus Phrasticus
26.description: No one has seen Phrastus the Scholar since his ill-advised return to the Imperial City. He's probably fine—he must be!—but in the meantime, his walled town house in Elinhir is available on an indefinite basis.

27.name: Strident Springs Demesne
27.description: This fortified manor between Arenthia and Skingrad at the headwaters of the Strid River should satisfy all those who aspire to the life of the landed gentry. Inside the gatehouse you'll find gardens, a waterfall, and a mansion in Second Empire style.

28.name: Autumn's-Gate
28.description: In the heart of The Rift, just outside the lively, small town of Nimalten, you will find this sturdy wooden home, with a large hearth to keep you warm in the Skyrim winter, and a stone wall to keep out the trolls.

29.name: Grymharth's Woe
29.description: Fine urban living in Windhelm is now available at this commodious town home, which features a lofty main floor, two fireplaces, and a second-floor balcony. Alas, that balcony lacks a railing, which is how Grymharth, after too much mead, came to woe.

30.name: Old Mistveil Manor
30.hint:
Gold Purchase Requires:
"The Rift Adventurer" Achievement
30.description: By tradition, the biggest mansion on the south side of Riften is always called Mistveil Manor. Since the death of old Thane Snelgar, the current Mistveil Estate has come available, including its impressive stone mansion with attached stable.

31.name: Hammerdeath Bungalow
31.description: "It may be small, but at least it's gloomy. And if you enjoy beating up on your friends, like I do, it's right next door to the arena!" —Goorguk gro-Murtag, Orcish Realtor

32.name: Mournoth Keep
32.description: This fortified household is strong, intimidating, and remote—in short, everything an Orc holds dear. And if you get tired of the "remote" part, there's a convenient wayshrine just outside your gate!

33.name: Forsaken Stronghold
33.description: When Hakkvild drove the Orcs of Yashnag's Kingdom out of Falkreath in 2E 467, the exiled Orsimer came east to establish Forsaken Stronghold. But the last Orcs died in 563 after they were visited by a merchant infected with Knahaten Flu.

34.name: Twin Arches
34.description: It may be small but it's solid, and it keeps the sandstorms out. The scenery is magnificent, but if you're in the mood for civilization, it's right outside the south gate of Hallin's Stand.

35.name: House of the Silent Magnifico
35.description: After the death of his beloved daughter Haruzeh at the Running of the Dunerippers, the Magnifico Z'za retired to his house in Sentinel and never spoke again, spending his last days playing endless games of hammergammon with his trained monkey, Lizard.

36.name: Hunding's Palatial Hall
36.description: This elegant pleasure palace, with its walled grounds enclosing stables, well, gardens, pool, watchtower, and docks, were paid for by the blood and treasure spilled from the countless treasure ships taken by the legendary Captain Izad.

37.name: Serenity Falls Estate
37.hint:
Gold Purchase Requires:
"Hero of the Aldmeri Dominion" Achievement
37.description: Set in a quiet corner of Reaper's March, the rural manor of Serenity Falls deserves its name, with plenty of room for servants and livestock, all behind a handsome wall to keep out the bandits and burglars.

38.name: Daggerfall Overlook
38.hint:
Gold Purchase Requires:
"Hero of the Daggerfall Covenant" Achievement
38.description: Before Daggerfall Castle was built, the kingdom's rulers lived in this imposing manor, now known as Daggerfall Overlook. The keep comes complete with a lower dungeon level.

39.name: Ebonheart Chateau
39.hint:
Gold Purchase Requires:
"Hero of the Ebonheart Pact" Achievement
39.description: A magnificent castle keep, complete with walls, watchtowers, well, fountain, and stable, all dramatically sited on the slopes of an active volcano! It just needs a murder, and then it will be haunted as well.

40.name: Grand Topal Hideaway
40.description: You probably think only the mad masterminds of vast criminal organizations have their own private tropical islands. Well, think again: you, too, could have a hidden hideaway ever-trembling on the verge of volcanic destruction!

41.name: Earthtear Cavern
41.description: You want privacy? What could be more private than lost and forgotten Nedic ruins in a remote corner of Craglorn's backcountry? Especially recommended for overthrown despots, retired master assassins, and Ministers of Finance exiled for embezzling.

42.name: Saint Delyn Penthouse
42.hint:
Purchase Requires:
"Room to Spare" House Quest Completion
42.description:
For the city-loving Dark Elf, there's no better choice of residence than the Saint Delyn Penthouse in the heart of Vivec City, on the Waistworks level of the Saint Delyn canton.
Room is too small for Dueling.

43.name: Amaya Lake Lodge
43.hint:
Gold Purchase Requires:
"Savior of Morrowind" Achievement
43.description: Enjoy the opulent luxury of a country lodge built by the Dark Elves of an earlier, more expansive era—a walled estate with a grand multistory house, roof balcony, stable, storage building, a well, and room for a formal garden.

44.name: Ald Velothi Harbor House
44.description: On the coast north of Gnisis, this three-level home in the Redoran "bug-house" style comes with a walled courtyard, a nearby dock, and convenient access to the nearby ruins of Ashalmawia and Arkngthunch-Sturdumz.

45.name: Tel Galen
45.description: Fulfill your fantasies of a fungal flat with this fabulous Telvanni wizard's tower, on a private island on Azura's Coast! Comes complete with grand foyer, workshop, suite, and tower chamber ideal for magical research.

46.name: Linchal Grand Manor
46.description: This imposing estate in the Nibenese style was originally built as the summer manor of an Imperial City nobleman, now sadly deceased. Gardens with statues and a reflecting pool surround the stately walled mansion. Sumptuous!

47.name: Coldharbour Surreal Estate
47.hint:
Gold Purchase Requires:
"The God of Schemes" Achievement
47.description: This overlooked acreage atop a floating plateau in Molag Bal's Oblivion realm of Coldharbour is available to be developed however you like. It's a secluded location, very quiet and private, even scenic in its own austere way.

48.name: Hakkvild's High Hall
48.hint:
Gold Purchase Requires:
"Horns of the Reach Delver" Achievement
48.description: Hakkvild, former Jarl of Falkreath who freed the hold from the hands of Yashnag's Orcs, built himself this spacious hall on the heights above town, with convenient access to the crypts of his ancestors. And now it can be yours!

49.name: Exorcised Coven Cottage
49.hint:
Gold Purchase Requires:
"An Unsparing Harvest" Achievement
Available During Witches Festival Only
49.description: Pay no attention to the rumors: this witches hut on the edge of Hag Fen in Glenumbra is guaranteed NOT to be haunted by the dead, the undead, or restless spirits of any kind. It does come with tumbledown walls to keep the crocodiles and wolves out. Spooky!

54.name: Pariah's Pinnacle
54.description: The grand and majestic mountaintop retreat of Baloth Bloodtusk was sealed off in the First Era by King Joile, but its ancient Orcish halls were recently reopened by order of King Kurog.

55.name: The Orbservatory Prior
55.description: Sotha Sil's designation of this mountaintop laboratory as the "Orbservatory Prior" clearly indicates that the site was an experimental or test version of what he had in mind—though whether he ever built an "Orbservatory Final" is unknown.

56.name: The Erstwhile Sanctuary
56.description: Built into the foundations of Kvatch itself, this ancient complex was abandoned by the Dark Brotherhood after a subterranean collapse tumbled one wall of the Speaker's bedchamber into a massive natural cavern.

57.name: Princely Dawnlight Palace
57.description: Prince Hubalajad, in one of his wilder flights of extravagance, had a second palace built solely to better catch the light of the morning sun. It's a magnificent estate that truly makes one feel like a monarch.

58.name: Golden Gryphon Garret
58.hint:
Purchase Requires:
"Room to Spare" House Quest Completion
58.description:
It's only a single room, but the advantage of this inn apartment is its unrivaled location, just steps from the gates of Alinor. That, and the rare prestige of an Alinor address!
Room is too small for Dueling.

59.name: Alinor Crest Townhouse
59.hint:
Gold Purchase Requires:
"Summerset Grand Adventurer" Achievement
59.description: On the heights of Alinor, with easy access to the Royal Palace, this splendid mansion was built as a consulate for the Bosmeri Ambassador of the Camoran Dynasty. With the ambassador now in Elden Root, the townhouse is available for you!

60.name: Colossal Aldmeri Grotto
60.description: Once a watering stop for the High Elf navy, this great cavernous grotto on the Summerset coast west of Dusk features shipboard compartments, magnificent Aldmeri ruins, weathered wood from several shipwrecks, and a sparkling subterranean waterfall.

61.name: Hunter's Glade
61.description: The underground entrance way leads through a portal to an expansive forested glade in Hircine's Oblivion realm of The Hunting Grounds. Those "blessed" with lycanthropy can maintain werewolf form indefinitely in this otherworldly wilderness.

62.name: Grand Psijic Villa
62.description: When Artaeum was "removed" from Tamriel, a few neighboring isles went with it, including the site of the Grand Psijic Villa, a monumental estate with magnificent views of the south coast of the main island.

63.name: Enchanted Snow Globe Home
63.description: Get small to go large: this miniature Snow Globe Home is tiny on the outside but expansive on the inside, proving shrunken real estate is a big bargain! And to make the interior cozier, the exterior features an eternally-festive gentle snowfall. Magical!

64.name: Lakemire Xanmeer Manor
64.description: Stay moist in an underwater Xanmeer Manor with its own submerged picture windows! Gaze into the depths of a lush Murkmire lake from the sunken interior of this capacious Argonian edifice, where comfort mixes casually with the bizarre. Xuth!

65.name: Frostvault Chasm
65.description: This side entrance to Frostvault leads down to a deep and spacious side grotto that was cut off from the main caverns long ago, though power still flows into it through conduits from the central source. Careful, those platforms have no handrails!

66.name: Elinhir Private Arena
66.description: Pit Fighting promoter Crottus "Thumbs-Down" Lycus built this private arena atop the haunted ruins of Molavar because the land was cheap, and what could go wrong? He vanished mysteriously some time ago, and now his unique Arena Home is back on the market.

68.name: Sugar Bowl Suite
68.hint:
Purchase Requires:
"Room to Spare" House Quest Completion
68.description:
Those seeking a respite from the heat and bustle of Rimmen's crowded streets can find it in this cozy suite. Easy access to Rimmen's amenities—both legal and illicit—make this the perfect abode for adventurers on the go.
Room is too small for Dueling.

69.name: Jode's Embrace
69.description: Few adeptoriums can match the hallowed majesty of Jode's Embrace. Rumor has it that the temple's worthiest occupants can peer into the sacred realm of Jode itself. Just keep an eye out for Dragons overhead!

70.name: Hall of the Lunar Champion
70.hint: Awarded for completing the "Two Queens" quest in Elsweyr.
70.description: The Khajiit of Elsweyr built this awesome temple as a tribute to the legendary hero, Khunzar-ri. Elsweyr's greatest champions may assume stewardship of the Hall, but only the most patient and cunning will discover all of its secrets!

71.name: Moon-Sugar Meadow
71.description: Dotted with Elsweyr architectural features, this meadow provides plenty of building space in a peaceful and natural setting. Nearby streams gleam in the light of the sun and moons, enhancing this idyllic getaway.

72.name: Wraithhome
72.description: With its pillars of skulls, stained glass, and ghostly portals, this abode can accommodate even the most tormented soul. Take advantage of its open layout to set up large-scale rituals, and use its vaults and lofty balconies for vile experiments.

73.name: Lucky Cat Landing
73.description: By some miracle or simple chance, Lucky Cat Landing weathered the fires that ravaged Southern Elsweyr completely unsinged! Its spacious terrace frames a gorgeous view, and its proximity to Senchal makes it convenient for those who enjoy city living.

74.name: Potentate's Retreat
74.description: Originally built by the Potentate Versidue-Shaie as a retreat from Senchal, this manor contains roomy spaces in which to entertain guests. A terraced area features a flooded aeonstone crater as well as luminescent flora transplanted from Moonlit Cove.

75.name: Forgemaster Falls
75.description: Thunderous waterfalls, an imposing smithy, and a magnificent view of the Great Bay make this brisk coastal village the perfect refuge for adventurers seeking a rugged Orcish lifestyle. |cFFFFFFIncludes a built-in blacksmithing station.|r

76.name: Thieves' Oasis
76.description: With its mix of Redguard architecture, both old and new, Thieves' Oasis features a stunning waterfall, ancient statues, and housing fit for a prince—whether that prince is a scholarly antiquarian or roguish thief.

77.name: Snowmelt Suite
77.hint:
Purchase Requires:
"Room to Spare" House Quest Completion
77.description:
Whether visiting the Bards College, seeking an audience at the Blue Palace, or looking to imbibe the best Nord mead around, take advantage of convenient living in the midst of Solitude with this room inside the Lonely Troll.
Room is too small for Dueling.

78.name: Proudspire Manor
78.hint:
Gold Purchase Requires:
"Skyrim Grand Adventurer" Achievement
78.description: Many lived within Solitude's coveted Proudspire Manor over the years, but its last owner vanished, leaving its spacious living quarters empty—and available. Shelter yourself from the cold within this multi-room landmark in the heart of Solitude.

79.name: Bastion Sanguinaris
79.description: Towering architecture, views to die (or kill) for, and a secret passage number among the many features of this striking Blackreach edifice, which stands within easy reach of Greymoor Keep.

80.name: Stillwaters Retreat
80.description: This Frozen Coast location features a Dwarven passage that leads past two deep alcoves and out to a frozen lake set amid the natural beauty of Skyrim. Hidden away beyond the lake, an ice cave awaits those seeking further respite from the world.

81.name: Antiquarian's Alpine Gallery
81.description: Tucked away in scenic Hjaalmarch, this rustic gallery contains plenty of space to display all manner of antiquities. A gorgeous waterfall provides water to a private pond, creating a perfect setting for scholarly gatherings.

82.name: Shalidor's Shrouded Realm
82.description: Before working arcane miracles on Eyevea and the College of Winterhold, the great mage Shalidor experimented with pocket realms of Oblivion. One domain, his Shrouded Realm, features Nord-style towers on arboreal terrain that floats in a wondrous sky.

83.name: Stone Eagle Aerie
83.description: From its majestic position above the city of Markarth, the Stone Eagle Aerie features breathtaking views, several water features, and sturdy Dwarven stonework. Rumors claim a hidden exit provides easy access to the Markarth Outlaws Refuge.

85.name: Kushalit Sanctuary
85.description: The recently abandoned Sheogorath shrine that locals call Assalkushalit features a statue to the Mad God within its stony hall. Whether you revere this Daedric Prince or want a home nestled in Red Mountain, this portal-ridden sanctuary can be yours!

86.name: Varlaisvea Ayleid Ruins
86.description: Ancient pillars along the Abecean Sea mark the site of once-soaring Ayleid architecture. Though none know the original purpose of these structures, some claim that soaking in the retreat's indoor crystal pool heals the spirit.

87.name: Pilgrim's Rest
87.hint:
Purchase Requires:
"Room to Spare" House Quest Completion
87.description:
Every year, hundreds of Zenithar's worshipers journey to Leyawiin, desperate for a glimpse of St. Kaladas's architectural marvel: The Great Chapel of Zenithar. This suite offers a welcome respite from the road's perils. 
Room is too small for dueling.

88.name: Water's Edge
88.hint:
Gold Purchase Requires:
"Blackwood Grand Adventurer" Achievement
88.description: Those seeking a taste of river life without all the flooding can find everything they need in this cozy bridge home. With both the Outlaws Refuge and Leyawiin Castle just a brief walk away, it's the perfect spot for nobles and lowlifes alike.

89.name: Pantherfang Chapel
89.description: The embattled clergy of the Quenching Grail established Pantherfang Chapel in the First Era as a bastion of faith. Part cathedral, part citadel, this edifice still stands as an immortal reminder of Aedric strength. Allows use of the Pledge of Mara.

90.name: Doomchar Plateau
90.description: Forged in the fires of the Deadlands, this lava-ringed plateau features a stunning view of Daedric landmarks and a solid foundation on which to build your very own Daedric dwelling. Live dangerously within the realm controlled by Prince Mehrunes Dagon!

91.name: Sweetwater Cascades
91.description: Set in an idyllic location between Khajiiti and Imperial lands, this tranquil villa draws upon the Anequina Aqueduct for its dancing fountains and deep cisterns. After relaxing outside, retreat indoors to enjoy healthy nourishment and restful sleep.

92.name: Ossa Accentium
92.description: Once the home of an eccentric merchant-collector, this sumptuous manor possesses a view framed by one of Fargrave's otherworldly skeletons plus offers easy access to all the amenities and exotic goods this city provides.

93.name: Agony's Ascent
93.description: Cautioning whispers about these dominating spires convince the wary to avoid the place for fear of torture … or worse. Those with courage, though, might find the stalwart tower and commanding views make for an imposing Oblivion keep.

94.name: Seaveil Spire
94.description: Early in the First Era, a pious tribe of Nedes followed the Tower's guidance to an undersea anomaly, where they built a submerged sanctuary. Millennia later, the edifice and anomaly remain, providing a secure and wondrous escape from the surface world.

95.name: Ancient Anchor Berth
95.hint:
Purchase Requires:
"Room to Spare" House Quest Completion
95.description:
Whether the bay's waters are tranquil or rough, you'll always find a spot of calm and warmth within the walls of this cozy inn room in Gonfalon Bay. Services abound just outside the door, making this a convenient berth.
Room is too small for dueling.

96.name: Highhallow Hold
96.description: Variously held by both House Dufort and Mornard, this stately manor near the edge of Gonfalon Bay is now available to the adventurer-about-town. It commands a majestic view of the water and provides easy access to the jewel of High Isle.

98.name: Fogbreak Lighthouse
98.description: The cozy life of a lighthouse keeper awaits any who claim Fogbreak as a home. This welcoming lighthouse includes a large undercroft, stunning views of the sea, a beacon to help ships navigate dangerous waters, and plenty of outdoor space to savor.

99.name: The Fair Winds
99.description: Enjoy sea-based living on the Fair Winds, a spacious galleon hailing from the Systres Isles. You have a bevy of travel options a mere spin of the ship's wheel away, with ports of call in Vulkhel Guard, Davon's Watch, and Daggerfall. Just watch for ornaugs!

100.name: Journey's End Lodgings
100.hint:
Purchase Requires:
"Room to Spare" House Quest Completion
100.description: Whether taking part in funerary rites or visiting the Dark Elf city of the dead, visitors to Necrom can rest easy within the confines of this spacious room inside the Mourner's Solace Inn. Full privacy—even from ancestral spirits—is guaranteed.

101.name: Emissary's Enclave
101.hint:
Gold Purchase Requires:
"Necrom Grand Adventurer" Achievement
101.description: Years ago, Tribunal priests requested a Necrom-based residence for an emissary and their staff. Today, this expansive home with scenic terraces is privately owned and seeks a caretaker—perhaps you—until an emissary of the Three needs it again.

102.name: Shadow Queen's Labyrinth
102.description: A winding maze dominates the grounds of this twilight-enshrouded estate, creating endless opportunities to perplex visitors. The visceral awe evoked by Nocturnal's Evergloam skies provides an exquisite contrast to the spacious, Summerset-inspired home.

103.name: Sword-Singer's Redoubt
103.description: Some claim the truest treasure in this former Sword-Singer stronghold glitters below ground in the form of cool, clear water. After the retreat of the Sword-Singers, enterprising merchants set up markets here for wealthy clients. Perhaps you will too?

104.name: Kelesan'ruhn
104.description: Designed by a mycoturge for a now-missing arcanist, this Telvanni-style residence showcases gorgeous views. Both magical and mundane access to a sizable workshop and a cozy living space allow for uninterrupted research and rejuvenating rest, respectively.

105.name: Gladesong Arboretum
105.description: The soothing sound of a waterfall accompanies the wind as it sings softly through the majestic trees in this druidic settlement. Carved stone shelters provide comfortable living spaces and open onto inspiring vistas.

106.name: Tower of Unutterable Truths
106.description: Only Hermaeus Mora knows why the previous curator fled this towering edifice filled with proscribed enigmata. Now the One Who Knows seeks a new cataloger who enjoys the panoptic views of Apocrypha and never, ever opens the books secured within.

107.name: Willowpond Haven
107.description: Twinkling candleflies and languorous willow trees set a cozy scene for this retreat nestled near a peaceful pond. Waterfalls and scenic views complete this serene living nook on the edge of Blackwood.

108.name: Zhan Khaj Crest
108.description: Breezes carry verdant scents from the nearby jungle to caress the sand gardens in this former Desert Wind adeptorium. Though no longer a site of Khajiit practicing a dual-sword technique, this riverside location serves well as a meditative getaway.

109.name: Rosewine Retreat
109.hint:
Purchase Requires:
"Room to Spare" House Quest Completion
109.description:
Once a favorite of wine merchants seeking to acquire the area's best vintages, this inn room can serve as a convenient refuge for any hoping to sample Skingrad's best food and drink.
Room is too small for dueling.

110.name: Merryvine Estate
110.hint:
Gold Purchase Requires:
"Gold Road Grand Adventurer" Achievement
110.description: Merryvine's wines once rivaled those of the nearby Valente Vineyard, but misfortune sent its former owner fleeing. This sun-kissed estate features fertile grapevines, a house suitable for entertaining, and facilities that would please any vintner.

111.name: Seabloom Villa
111.description: Blossom lovers will delight in this picturesque villa perched on the western coastline of Auridon! With its elegant design, this cozy home awaits any who seek to nurture its blooms to life while enjoying how the light dances on the nearby rippling waters.

112.name: Haven of the Five Companions
112.hint: Acquired through purchase, promotion, or event.
112.description: Originally the sanctuary for the Five Companions, this stately structure features five rooms—one for each of the original Companions—plus a central meeting space. Gorgeous views of West Weald and Cyrodiil complement the majestic serenity of this area.

113.name: Kthendral Deep Mines
113.description: Glowing crystals dot the walls of this abandoned Dwarven processing facility perched over fathomless mines in Blackreach. Smiths and others who require steady heat for forging materials can use the active furnace to craft wondrous creations.

114.name: Grand Gallery of Tamriel
114.description: Once the primary museum for collections curated by the University of Gwylim, this stately structure and its grounds provide a perfect setting for the display of art, curios, statuary, and more. Show off favored possessions in a refined locale!

115.name: Shattered Mirror Isle
115.description: Scintillating islands and skeletons of long-forgotten beasts float amid Mirrormoor's luminous skies. Enterprising architects, step through a shattered mirror portal in Fargrave and finesse this osseous mass into a dazzling dimensional home.

116.name: Castle Skingrad
116.description: Count Calantius cordially invites a caretaker to maintain and decorate Castle Skingrad as he rides out to support his loyal citizens. This majestic castle stands just outside Skingrad, granting easy access to the city's amenities and nearby vineyards.

117.name: Bismuth Steam Baths
117.hint:
Gold Purchase Requires:
"West Solstice Grand Adventurer" Achievement
117.description: Once a relaxing getaway for Corelanyan nobles, this elegant retreat features an outdoor pool along the shore, indoor steam baths, and spacious facilities that allow even the most battle-worn adventurer to treat themselves.

118.name: The Sleepy Sloth
118.hint:
Purchase Requires:
"Room to Spare" House Quest Completion
118.description: Named after an amusing incident with Solstice's sloths, this airy room provides travelers and adventurers alike with a quiet space to recuperate. It can even accommodate your favorite arboreal friends!

119.name: Theater of the Ancestors
119.description: An entertainer's delight! Plays, recitals, and more once filled the stage in this Ayleid theater—all dedicated to Merid-Nunda, the Bright One. Tucked away in the Colored Rooms, this opulent venue awaits its next riveting performance and adoring patrons.

120.name: Hiddenspring Cottage
120.description: Bucolic comfort awaits! This cozy cottage nestled among stalwart trees and bubbling brooks provides a charming escape from the strife of the outside world. Grab a book, pack a picnic basket, and let nature enfold you in its many wonders.

121.name: Wildgrown Chapel of Julianos
121.description: Twisted by magical growth, a crumbling chapel to the God of Wisdom and Logic now hangs above the river Strid. A nearby Colovian manor house provides shelter from the elements for any who dare rest within this tangle of restless greenery.

122.name: Cradle of the Worm Colossus
122.description: Discovered by guild mages in the aftermath of the Writhing Wall campaign, this dread realm hosts a bone colossus personally crafted by Wormblood. Wrest this stronghold from the worms and use the colossus to practice your best combat moves!

123.name: Druidspring Conservatory
123.description: Experience all of Y'ffre's seasons in a single day! This estate blends a Druid-crafted four-season garden and the beauty of a Breton's noble villa. Grab a trowel and start making this garden getaway your own!

124.name: Night's Den
124.description: The Night Market provides vast opportunities, including a former bank vault in need of a new owner. Hoard your wealth—and your faction's secrets—inside. Plus decorate your den with faction furnishings as you gain favor with your chosen group!

125.name: Buccaneer Bay
125.description: Need a friendly port in a hurry? Escape to Buccaneer Bay! Forget your woes (or let your woes forget you) in a sunny seaside setting. And don't worry about raiders. Stories of ghost pirates lurking in the depths keep them away.

1133.description: In Imperial City Prison, defeat the Overfiend, Ibomez the Flesh Sculptor, the Gravelight Sentry, the Flesh Abomination, and Lord Warden Dusk without any group member being noticed by the Vigilant Watchers.

1142.name: Darklight Dancer
1142.description: Defeat the Lord Warden Dusk of Imperial City Prison while you and your group members avoid every Darklight Burst.

1303.name: Lord Warden's Retaliation
1303.description: In Veteran Imperial City Prison, destroy the Warden's Tome, then defeat Lord Warden Dusk.

1345.name: Imperial City Prison Vanquisher
1345.description: Defeat the Overfiend, Ibomez the Flesh Sculptor, the Gravelight Sentry, the Flesh Abomination, the Lord Warden's Council, and Lord Warden Dusk in the Imperial City Prison.

1120.name: White-Gold Tower Conqueror
1120.description: Defeat the Adjudicator, the Elite Guard, the Planar Inhibitor, and Molag Kena in Veteran White-Gold Tower.

1132.name: Imperial City Challenger
1132.description: Complete the listed Challenges for veteran dungeons in Imperial City.

1275.name: First to the Top
1275.description: Defeat the Adjudicator, the Empress Regent's Guard, the Planar Inhibitor, and Molag Kena in Veteran White-Gold Tower within 30 minutes of starting the dungeon. Timer starts when you enter Green Emperor Way.

1276.name: To Spite a Tharn
1276.description: Defeat the Adjudicator, the Empress Regent's Guard, the Planar Inhibitor, and Molag Kena in Veteran White-Gold Tower without experiencing the death of a group member.

1277.name: Horn Breaker
1277.description: Defeat 100 Xivkyn in Veteran White-Gold Tower.

1278.name: Daedroth Dropper
1278.description: Defeat 75 Daedroth in Veteran White-Gold Tower.

1279.name: Ire of the Storm
1279.description: In Veteran White-Gold Tower, complete the ritual listed in the Obelisk Tome, then defeat Molag Kena.

1280.name: Entry Denied
1280.description: In Veteran White-Gold Tower, destroy all portals to prevent the arrival of the Planar Inhibitor's reinforcements.

1281.name: Imperial Transgressions
1281.description: Locate and interact with all of the speaking stones in the White-Gold Tower.

1306.name: Out of the Frying Pan
1306.description: In Veteran White-Gold Tower, become completely engulfed in flame by the Planar Inhibitor's Heat Stroke attack before it completes its Daedric Catastrophe attack. Then stay alive until the Planar Inhibitor is defeated.

1346.name: White-Gold Tower Vanquisher
1346.description: Defeat the Adjudicator, the Elite Guard, the Planar Inhibitor, and Molag Kena in White-Gold Tower.

1.description: Handsome, strong, and swift, the palomino is favored by couriers and sportsmen.
1.name: Palomino Horse

2.description: A hardy, well-rounded, and dependable beast.
2.name: Sorrel Horse
2.hint: Acquired from the level up advisor.

3.description: Favored by farmers and traders, this muscular horse is strong and patient.
3.name: Brown Paint Horse
3.hint: Purchased from the Stablemasters located in cities throughout Tamriel.

4.description: This energetic mount is well-liked by battlefield scouts.
4.name: Bay Dun Horse
4.hint: Purchased from the Stablemasters located in cities throughout Tamriel.

5.description: A luxurious black steed, often considered a point of pride and distinction by Tamrielic jockeys, cavalry, and couriers.
5.name: Midnight Steed
5.hint: Purchased from the Stablemasters located in cities throughout Tamriel.

6.description: Impetuous and fierce, this all-purpose Imperial steed yields only to a capable master.
6.name: Imperial Horse

7.description: A frisky little crustacean pal, at home in the water or out of it.
7.name: Nibenay Mudcrab

8.description: A loyal steam-powered Dwarven Spider, fueled by magicka from a soul gem that will last for eras.
8.name: Razak's Opus
8.hint: Acquired by completing the quest "The Mystery of Razak."

9.description: A favorite household pet in Morrowind, the Pony Guar is a glutton for affection.
9.name: Pony Guar

10.description: The caramel scrib crony is a quiet companion, devoted and easily housebroken.
10.name: Crony Scrib

11.description: The imgakin monkey pet is lively and cheerful, even in the grimmest of dungeons.
11.name: Imgakin Monkey
11.hint: Acquired by playing in The Elder Scrolls Online Beta.

12.description: The hunting dog of the Nords of Skyrim, known to face down sabre cats for their masters.
12.name: Whiterun Wolfhound

13.description: A perky crab buddy whose rust-colored shell covers a cheerful, inquisitive demeanor.
13.name: Rufous Mudcrab

14.description: This cross between a domestic pig and a Skyrim boar is as loyal as it is adorable.
14.name: Bristlegut Piglet

15.description: This lambent little larva loves crawling alongside valorous adventurers!
15.name: Frisky Scrib

16.description: An ice wraith from the slopes of the highest mountain in Tamriel.
16.name: High Hrothgar Wraith
16.hint: This unique pet is granted as a token of appreciation to players who remained subscribed to The Elder Scrolls Online for three months.

17.description: A Dwarven Sphere of the long-lost Dwemer.
17.name: Loyal Dwarven Sphere
17.hint: This unique pet is granted as a token of appreciation to players who remained subscribed to The Elder Scrolls Online for six months.

18.description: The robust Green Narsis is the standard mount and dray-beast of central Morrowind.
18.name: Green Narsis Guar

19.description: A crossbreed of banded and wild guar, as fearsome as it is intelligent and difficult to control.
19.name: Golden Eye Guar

20.description: A breed of guar bred for cavalry use, able to carry an armored warrior into battle.
20.name: Banded Guar Charger

21.description: A sturdy, multi-purpose guar, at home anywhere from swamps to the ashlands.
21.name: Tessellated Guar

22.description: A mount bred for bearing an armed warrior while slinking through the steamy jungles of Pellitine.
22.name: Senche-Leopard

23.description: A strong yet nimble mount, bred for hunting in the Tenmar forest.
23.name: Clouded Senche-Leopard

24.description: A mount said to have been bred by Baandari Pedlars for ease in hastily leaving town after dark.
24.name: Black Senche-Panther

25.description: These fierce and powerful mounts hail from the broad savannahs of Anequina.
25.name: Senche-Lioness

26.description: Though unwilling to fight, this Daedric minion will follow you loyally—for now.
26.name: Banekin

27.description: This busy little buddy is sometimes mistaken for an imgakin monkey.
27.name: Blackwood Monkey

28.description: A reptilian pal from Morrowind, where they're known for quickness, devotion, and a mildly offensive odor.
28.name: Vermilion Scuttler
28.hint: Obtained by pre-purchasing the Explorer's Pack.

29.description: The Bravil Retriever loves the water and is a favorite hunter's companion from Anvil to Gideon.
29.name: Bravil Retriever

30.description: Some scholars believe Argonians are descended—or were uplifted—from these tree-dwelling swamp lizards. True or not, they make great pets, affectionate and low-maintenance.
30.name: Helstrom Ancestor Lizard

31.description: A foul-smelling Daedric minion, who will follow you loyally, though it won't fight for you.
31.name: Daedric Scamp

32.description: Descended from royal hunting dogs, Windhelm Wolfhounds are known as steadfast companions.
32.name: Windhelm Wolfhound

33.description: This green-eyed feline is a distant relative of the Alfiq Khajiit.
33.name: Housecat

34.description: This guise causes the user to take on the appearance of a living skeleton.
34.name: Skeleton
34.hint: Acquired by completing the quest "The Bargain's End."

35.description: A semi-domesticated version of the wild senche-tiger, this distant relative of the Khajiit has been bred for size and manageability.
35.name: Striped Senche-Tiger
35.hint: This unique mount was granted as a token of appreciation to players who remained subscribed to The Elder Scrolls Online from April 2014 through June 2015.

37.description: Often accompanying ships as they leave port, each blue-purple iridescent Dovah-Fly chooses a person to follow. Each night, the whirr of its gently flitting wings pull its chosen one to slumber, and at sunrise it lightly lands on its "pet" to wake them up.
37.name: Sea Sapphire Dovah-Fly

38.description: This heavy leather smith's apron and gauntlets denotes a master of the forge.
38.name: Blacksmith

39.description: A high-end chef's outfit that indicates the wearer is a provisioner supreme.
39.name: Chef

40.description: This jovial jester garb, including mask and bell-cap, could even make a zombie smile.
40.name: Royal Court Jester

41.description: Many a Vvardenfell youngster growing up in the swamps of West Gash or the Bitter Coast remembers spending happy hours playing "dodge-dovah" with these hovering bug-buddies! If hand-raised from larval form, they can become devoted companion animals.
41.name: Regal Dovah-Fly

43.description: This scurrying vermin from Oblivion would be lost in the vastness of Nirn without a loyal companion and guide. Even a Daedric rodent needs a friend.
43.name: Daedrat

44.description: When a member of the Elder Council must go to war, he or she dons the traditional armor of the Imperial Chancellor.
44.name: Imperial Chancellor

46.description: When rounding up criminal scum or raiding hives of heresy in the dark of night, the Temple's Ordinators don this night-dark armor.
46.name: Ordinator Night-Raid Armor

47.description: All hail <<player{his/her}>> Imperial Majesty, Emperor of Cyrodiil!
47.name: Emperor's Regalia
47.hint: Acquired by becoming the Emperor of Cyrodiil.

48.description: This guise enables its wearer to assume the grim aspect of a Dark Seducer.
48.name: Dark Seducer

49.description: The wearer of this guise looks exactly like one of Sheogorath's dreaded Golden Saints.
49.name: Golden Saint

50.description: One can sneer at lesser mortals when wearing this exact replica of the regalia of the King of Worms.
50.name: Mannimarco

51.description: This guise makes the wearer appear to have withered flesh beneath ancient Nord armor—perfect for lurking in tombs.
51.name: Draugr
